subject: Exception conditions
notes: kb/Work PB77 + PB75 (2026-08-18): with checking for a fatal exception condition NOT enabled 'the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected'. WiseOwl COBOL's determination for the arithmetic size error condition without a SIZE ERROR phrase (EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, §14.7.5 no-phrase rule 4; A.1 item 70): execution continues and the resultant identifier receives the LOW-ORDER digits of the result aligned at its scale (CobolNum.Store's high-order truncation), for EVERY value carrier — SDIDI (CobolDec.ToUnscaled, PB74), the native exact family (CobolNum.RescaleStoreCap's high-order truncation), a binary64 (ToScaledUnchecked / FromDouble's unchecked form — the exact decimal expansion past the Int128 carrier). A non-finite binary64 landing in a fixed-point receiver stores ZERO. An INTERMEDIATE that cannot be formed at all (a standard-decimal intermediate past decimal128, a native value past the Int128 escape boundary in a value-semantics position, an exponentiation-rule violation, a zero divisor) has no result: execution does NOT continue — the run unit terminates abnormally, exit 1, naming the condition (PB75; it used to be a raw CLR crash, exit 127). Documented on CONFORMANCE.md (the item-70 row). The compiled path (review findings w1154a R1-1, R1-3): CommitRollbackRefusalWitnessTests compiles and runs the program over the refusing medium, so item 8 is pinned after a refused COMMIT or ROLLBACK of the element's own file and of another element's file, and after an ordinary statement's fatal status on a file under commit control. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#Rescaled (kb/Work PB3839 deleted CobolIntrinsics.Rescaled with the last Int128 NUMVAL-F body: NUMVAL, NUMVAL-C and NUMVAL-F are all SDIDI functions now (IntrinsicCarrierRules.ReturnsExactParse), and the Int128 landing helper had no other caller)
